questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes a loop diuretic from disease-modifying HFrEF therapy?
choices: It replaces the need for all other HFrEF medications
It primarily relieves congestion but does not by itself replace outcome-improving therapy
It is used only to slow atrial fibrillation
It has no effect on volume status
questions.explanation: Loop diuretics promote sodium and water excretion and commonly relieve congestion. They do not by themselves replace evidence-based therapies intended to improve long-term HFrEF outcomes.

questions.question: Why do MRAs require potassium and renal-function monitoring?
choices: They always cause low potassium
They can reduce aldosterone-mediated potassium secretion and increase hyperkalemia risk
They have no renal effects
They are used only for chest pain
questions.explanation: MRAs counter aldosterone signaling. Because aldosterone promotes renal potassium secretion, MRAs can raise potassium, especially with CKD or other potassium-raising medications.

questions.question: A patient with HFrEF has rapidly worsening dyspnea at rest, hypotension, confusion, and cool extremities. What is the safest FNP response?
choices: Increase the home diuretic and reassess next month
Recognize possible acute decompensation or hypoperfusion and arrange emergency evaluation
Start an antianginal medication without examination
Wait for a daily weight next week
questions.explanation: Dyspnea at rest with hypotension, confusion, and cool extremities can signal unstable acute heart failure or shock. This requires emergency-level assessment rather than routine outpatient titration.

questions.question: What is the key safety concern when nitrates are combined with phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors?
choices: Profound hypotension
Hyperkalemia
Agranulocytosis
Thyroid storm
questions.explanation: The combination can produce dangerous additive vasodilation and profound hypotension. Patients need explicit medication-specific counseling.

questions.question: Which is the best first conceptual step when treating atrial fibrillation?
choices: Assume every patient needs the same antiarrhythmic
Assess whether the rhythm is causing hemodynamic instability
Prescribe anticoagulation without risk assessment
Treat the ECG instead of the patient
questions.explanation: In AF, first determine stability. Hypotension, ischemic chest discomfort, shock, altered mental status, or acute pulmonary edema changes urgency and management.

questions.question: Why can nondihydropyridine calcium channel blockers require caution in certain patients with HFrEF?
choices: They may reduce contractility
They always cause severe hypertension
They increase ejection fraction in every patient
They are anticoagulants
questions.explanation: These medications can have negative inotropic effects, so rate-control medication choice must consider ventricular function and overall hemodynamics.

questions.question: Which factor is essential to an anticoagulation decision for atrial fibrillation?
choices: Only whether the rhythm is irregular
Validated stroke-risk assessment together with bleeding, organ-function, medication, and valve context
The patient’s favorite medication color
A single normal blood pressure reading
questions.explanation: Anticoagulation decisions are individualized. Stroke risk, bleeding risk, kidney/liver function, interactions, valve context, adherence, and current guidance all matter.

questions.question: A patient with previously stable exertional angina now has persistent chest pressure at rest with diaphoresis and nausea. What is the appropriate interpretation?
choices: Routine stable angina that can wait for a refill
Possible acute coronary syndrome requiring urgent evaluation
Expected effect of statin therapy
A reason to increase exercise intensity
questions.explanation: New, persistent, accelerating, or rest chest symptoms with concerning associated findings can represent acute coronary syndrome and must not be managed as routine chronic angina.

questions.question: Which statement about SGLT2 inhibitors in heart failure is most accurate?
choices: They replace all other heart-failure medications
Selected agents may provide heart-failure benefit in appropriate patients, with individualized safety review
They are used only for acute chest pain
They require no review of volume status or adverse effects
questions.explanation: Selected SGLT2 inhibitors have heart-failure benefits in appropriate patients, but selection and monitoring remain individualized and include volume, kidney, acute-illness, and medication-safety considerations.

questions.question: Why is medication reconciliation especially important in heart failure and arrhythmia care?
choices: OTC and duplicate therapies cannot affect cardiovascular medications
NSAIDs, potassium products, duplicate nodal blockers, stimulants, and missed medications can worsen hemodynamics or create adverse effects
It is relevant only at hospital discharge
It replaces assessing symptoms and vital signs
questions.explanation: Medication interactions and omissions commonly worsen heart failure or arrhythmias. A full prescription, OTC, supplement, and outside-prescriber review is a core safety intervention.
